title: Classroom or online?
context_es: En clase habéis hablado de las distintas formas de estudiar. Tu profesor te pide un ensayo, como en la Parte 1 del Writing de B2 First.
prompt_en:
In your English class you have been talking about different ways of studying. Now your teacher has asked you to write an essay.

Is it better to learn in a classroom than to study online?

Notes
Write about:
1. flexibility
2. contact with other people
3. your own idea
useful_language: To sum up, although …, I believe that …
tips_es: Estructura: introducción, un párrafo por nota (las dos dadas y la tuya) y conclusión con tu opinión.
Registro formal: sin contracciones ni exclamaciones, y con conectores (*However, In addition, Therefore*).
La tercera nota es tuya: elige una idea distinta de las otras dos y desarróllala igual.
model_answer:
In recent years, studying online has become very popular, and many people wonder whether traditional classrooms are still necessary. In my view, both options have clear advantages, although one of them suits most learners better.

The main benefit of online courses is flexibility. Students can follow a lesson whenever they have time, which is ideal for people who work or have children. In a classroom, by contrast, everybody has to be in the same place at the same time.

However, contact with other people is much richer face to face. In a classroom, students can ask questions immediately, work in pairs and learn from the mistakes of their classmates. Online, it is easy to feel alone, even with a chat or a forum.

Another point to consider is motivation. Without a teacher and a fixed timetable, many learners stop after a few weeks. Having a class to attend makes it harder to give up.

To sum up, although online courses are convenient, I believe that learning in a classroom is more effective for most people, because it provides the human contact and the routine that keep us studying.
